title: Run Mana's tool loop on DeepSeek and meter what it costs
body:
Part of #1406 (1 of 4). The self-work ladder, chat-on-request and the Settings section build on this.

- **Remote tool loop.** `runtime.remoteToolReply({ baseUrl, apiKey, model, thinking })` runs her existing tool loop on an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. All of her helpers stay the same (prompts, tool-call repair, goal review, context guard); only the request is swapped.
  - The key goes in a header, never in a log.
  - The tier sets the model and thinking. No local sampling settings are sent.
  - Each earlier turn's `reasoning_content` is sent back while tools are on, which DeepSeek's thinking mode requires (it returns a 400 otherwise).
  - Local-only mode refuses it before anything is sent.
  - The prompt-size guard reads the API's `usage` when there are no llama timings.
- **API spending (`api-spending.js`).** One bucket per day, model and use (self-work, chat, bench), holding tokens and dollars:
  - tokens: input from cache, input not from cache, output, and the reasoning part of output;
  - dollars at DeepSeek's prices, doubled in its weekday peak windows;
  - a model without known prices shows tokens only;
  - no prompts or code are ever stored.
  - Exposed through `GET /api-spending` for Settings and the `api_spending__summary` chat tool (read tier).
- **DeepSeek key.** `GET/POST /self-work/escalation` store the key protected, like the other keys, and only ever return `hasKey`. Escalation is off by default.

Tests:
- `api-spending.test.js`: peak windows, the cost split, totals by period, model and use, restart survival, and the chat tool.
- `remote-tool-loop.test.js`: endpoint, key, model and thinking in the request; reasoning sent back or not; usage reaching `onResponse`; local-only and missing-key refusals.
- `escalation-routes.test.js`: the key is never returned, and the spending route works.
interface: The merged change for PR #1412 is covered by test/api-spending.test.js, test/escalation-routes.test.js, test/remote-tool-loop.test.js.
why: Additional real merged-fix benchmark case selected to broaden the agentic coding evaluation.
